heroSub: 10 Khon Kaen hotels people talk about most and that we've reviewed in depth — a 5-star luxury hotel with a huge convention centre, big-room downtown hotels near Central, boutiques within walking distance of the train station, all the way to a cafe resort on the Nam Phong river near Ubolratana Dam. introH2: 🏙️ What kinds of hotels does Khon Kaen have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Khon Kaen is the hub city of Isan, and people come here for very different reasons — some for conferences and seminars, some to drop a kid off at university or visit relatives at Khon Kaen University, some for the nightlife on Khao Niao Road, and some just need a stopover while road-tripping around Isan. So the city's accommodation doesn't have a single face — it ranges from a 5-star luxury hotel with one of the region's largest convention centres, to an old downtown hotel with big rooms a short walk from Central, to a small boutique you can walk to the train station from, all the way to a cafe resort on the Nam Phong river that means driving out of town. A lot of people pick a place that doesn't match their trip, and end up with an inconvenient location or paying more than they needed to. This article rounds up 10 popular Khon Kaen hotels we've reviewed in depth — luxury picks, value big-room picks, budget options, and a riverside resort. Every one comes from reading real guest reviews, with both the upsides and the honest caveats, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links for all of them.
mrtHtml: Khon Kaen has no metro; getting around town by Grab or songthaew (shared truck) is easy and cheap. There are several ways to reach Khon Kaen — by air, landing at Khon Kaen Airport (KKC), about 1 hour from Bangkok and roughly a 10–15 min drive into the city; by train, getting off at Khon Kaen station right in the centre, with some hotels within walking distance; by bus or self-drive, taking Mittraphap Road from Bangkok in about 6–7 hours. The main accommodation areas in this article: Si Chan Road / Khao Niao Road in the city centre, next to Central and the nightlife zone, walkable to everything; Prachasamoson Road / Prachasamran Road, close to the centre but away from the bustle, with plenty of parking; near the train station, good if you arrive by rail; and Ubolratana District, out of town to the north about a 50 min drive, for resorts by the dam.

entries.name: Avani Khon Kaen Hotel & Convention Centre
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Prachasamoson Road · ~1 km to the walking street
entries.addr: 999 Moo 4, Prachasamoson Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen
entries.storyHtml: Ask people in Khon Kaen which luxury hotel comes to mind first for conferences, seminars, or weddings, and many give the same answer: Avani Khon Kaen. It's a 5-star hotel under Minor Hotels' Avani brand on Prachasamoson Road, open since 2012 — formerly the Pullman before it joined the Avani group. Among the 10 hotels we reviewed, it has the highest score at 9.5 from 283 Trip.com reviews. What keeps it in almost every conversation about luxury stays in Khon Kaen is its convention centre of over 4,000 square metres, with 11 breakout rooms, one of the largest event spaces in the Isan region, which keeps the lobby busy and lively. From real reviews, the people it suits best are business travellers, conference and seminar attendees, and families who want a full-service hotel with a pool for the kids and plenty of parking. The entry-level Avani Room is roomy enough for two without feeling cramped, and reviews agree the rooms are very clean, the beds are softer and more comfortable than expected, and the soundproofing is fairly good. Where many say the upgrade is worth it is the Skyline rooms, which come with Club Lounge access — unlimited snacks, drinks, and an evening happy hour. The breakfast buffet draws praise for its variety and the local Isan dishes you don't often find in big chain hotels, giving you a taste of the province from the first meal. There's an outdoor pool with a kids' section that has a slide, the Avani Spa, a fitness centre, a sauna, and a large free car park with complimentary valet that reviews call rare for a city hotel. Honest caveats from the reviews: the building has been open since 2012, and some corners and unrenovated rooms don't look as new as a brand-new hotel; during big events the lobby and car park get crowded, restaurant service can be slow during festivals, and some rooms booked as a King come with two single beds pushed together. Bottom line — among Khon Kaen's accessible luxury hotels, Avani is still a top pick that's hard to match in this province.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're here to work or staying several nights, consider a Skyline room with Club Lounge access — the price difference is small but you get snacks and happy hour all day. And check the hotel's event calendar before booking; during a big seminar or wedding, ask for a high floor away from the event zone for quiet.

Convention centre over 4,000 sqm with 11 meeting rooms, one of the largest in Isan
Varied breakfast buffet with local Isan dishes · pool with a kids' section
Large free car park with valet · accessible price for an international 5-star chain

entries.name: The Heritage Grand Khon Kaen Hotel and Convention
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.7 · over 1,000 reviews · former Pullman Raja Orchid building
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Prachasamran Road · walk to Central Plaza
tags: 📐 Rooms from 43 sqm up to 84 sqm suites
entries.addr: 9/9 Prachasamran Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen
entries.storyHtml: Anyone who visited Khon Kaen more than a decade ago probably remembers this tall building on Prachasamran Road, because it's the same one as the Pullman Khon Kaen Raja Orchid that stood with the city for years before changing ownership and rebranding as The Heritage Grand Khon Kaen. That's important to know before booking, because old and new reviews are mixed together across several sites — some still use the Pullman name — so when reading, check the review dates. To put it plainly, this is a hotel with good bones: a large building, big rooms, and full facilities like a grand hotel of the old days, but its age is starting to show with time. The real star is the genuinely spacious rooms, starting at 43 square metres, clearly bigger than many same-class hotels in the city, which often give a standard room of around 28–32 sqm — here it's 43 sqm from the cheapest room, scaling up to an 84 sqm suite. Many rooms look out over the city or Bueng Kaen Nakhon lake; rooms have a bathtub separate from the shower, and several reviews praise the soundproofing, which masks the noise from the nightlife area around the hotel reasonably well. The best fit is people here to work, attend conferences, and families who want a big room near the mall, since it's an easy walk to Central Plaza and Fairy Plaza. The signature feature reviews mention often is the in-house brewhouse, Kronen Brauhaus, with its own draft beer and live music almost every night — sometimes featuring a ranat ek (Thai xylophone) player — plus a bakery many call a hidden find. Honest caveats: the building has age and is being renovated in stages, so room condition isn't consistent — some get a renovated room and love it, others get an original room with old furniture; water pressure is weak in some rooms, and some reviews say the nightlife noise around the hotel carries until 2 a.m. If you value space and location over a fresh interior, this is good value and a solid fit at around two thousand a night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a renovated room when booking or at check-in, since condition varies, and if the price difference is small, choose a Bueng Kaen Nakhon lake-view room over a city view. Light sleepers should request a high floor facing away from the entertainment street, and don't miss the bakery and the Kronen Brauhaus brewhouse.

entries.name: Glacier Hotel Khon Kaen
entries.badge: 🚂 Walk to the train station · big rooms
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pracha Samran Road · walk to the City Pillar Shrine + train station
tags: 🏙️ City centre, walk to the train station
🛏️ Big rooms from ~32 sqm, strong cold AC
entries.addr: 141 Pracha Samran Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen
entries.storyHtml: If you come to Khon Kaen and want a city-centre location within walking distance of the City Pillar Shrine, the train station, and the nightlife zone, all at a price that doesn't reach the high thousands, Glacier Hotel Khon Kaen is a name guests bring up often. It's a 4-star boutique hotel on Pracha Samran Road, open since 2010 and with rooms renovated in 2023, scoring 8.9 from 476 reviews. The hotel has a cool white design concept, with a small waterfall at the entrance leading into a glass-walled lobby. The number-one selling point that pushes its location score to 9.3 is exactly that — location. Several international reviews note that it's only about a 6-minute walk from Khon Kaen train station to the hotel, so people arriving by rail don't need to pay for onward transport; the City Pillar Shrine is about a 500-metre walk away, and Central Plaza is about 1 km. The people it suits are travellers here on city business, conference-goers, families dropping off or visiting a student at Khon Kaen University, and those stopping a night or two before moving on. What makes this hotel talked about is that the rooms are far bigger than hotels at a similar price — the Deluxe starts at around 32 sqm with a big bed — and the thing guests most consistently praise is the strong, cold air-conditioning, which matters a lot for Isan's hot season when it hits 38–40 degrees. Another thing rare at this price is the indoor pool, usable without worrying about sun or rain, plus free parking. Service is a strength that draws steady praise, with friendly, helpful staff. Honest caveats: room quality isn't consistent — unrenovated rooms may have a rusty showerhead, weak water flow, or a showerhead mounted too low to use comfortably; the AC in some rooms can't be set cold enough all the time; some rooms have windows that don't open; and the pool water is sometimes cloudy from inconsistent upkeep. If you book a renovated room and set expectations right, this is a fitting, good-value pick at around the low thousands.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a renovated room (Premium or Grand Deluxe) right at booking, since room quality varies. If you arrive by train, you can walk from the station straight to the hotel; if you sleep lightly, ask for an interior or high-floor room; and if you plan to use the pool, check the water condition before getting in.

entries.storyHtml: Ask people in Khon Kaen about a big downtown hotel, and Charoen Thani Hotel Khon Kaen is often one of the first names that comes to mind. It's a 4-star, 320-room city hotel on Si Chan Road, and one of the long-established hotels locals have known for years, scoring 8.4 from more than four thousand reviews — a trustworthy number for a hotel in the low-thousands price range. The number-one selling point is location — it's about a 300-metre walk to Khao Niao Road, Khon Kaen's famous nightlife strip, and close to Central Plaza, roughly a 10-minute walk or a short 5-minute drive, with a location score in real reviews as high as 9.2. The hotel is surrounded by restaurants, cafes, markets, and convenience stores, so you barely need to plan where to eat. The best fit is people here on city business, conference-goers, those out for the nightlife, or groups and families who value location and convenience over how new the rooms are. As a 320-room hotel it has many room types, and rooms are larger than the typical city hotel, accommodating several people. Breakfast comes up often and positively, especially the kai krata, a signature upper-Isan breakfast dish served hot in a small pan. There's an outdoor pool, fitness centre, spa, two restaurants, a bar, and free parking that's valuable in a downtown location. Service scores well at around 8.8, with friendly staff who help quickly in the warm style of an older Thai hotel. Honest caveats: the building and furniture are starting to age — some reviews mention old bathtub tiles with slight water seepage, too few power outlets to charge several devices, dust in the corners of some rooms, a dated-looking pool, and a poolside bar that's sometimes closed; and street-facing rooms may hear noise from Khao Niao Road on Friday and Saturday nights. Bottom line — if you plan to use the hotel as a base for exploring the city on foot, every baht you pay for this location comes back in full.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Specify a renovated room when booking, since room condition in an old hotel clearly varies. Choose a package that includes breakfast, since the morning buffet is a strength — don't skip the kai krata — and if you sleep lightly, ask for an interior room not facing Khao Niao Road.

cons: Building and furniture starting to age; bathtub tiles in some rooms seep water
Few power outlets in the rooms · dated-looking pool, poolside bar sometimes closed

entries.name: B2 Khon Kaen Boutique & Budget Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 In the city, near Bueng Kaen Nakhon · 3 min to Central
tags: 📍 Near Bueng Kaen Nakhon · 3 min to Central
entries.addr: 444 Moo 4, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen
entries.storyHtml: If you're on a tight budget but want a city-centre location, B2 Khon Kaen Boutique & Budget Hotel is the straightforward answer — a 3-star hotel from B2, a Thai budget chain with dozens of branches across the country, scoring 7.9 from 827 reviews. The brand's formula is very simple: clean rooms, comfy beds, cold air-conditioning, a light price, with the extras like a fancy lobby, a big restaurant, or a pool cut to keep the price as low as possible. The Khon Kaen branch has a location advantage, sitting in the city, about 2.1 km from Bueng Kaen Nakhon and just a 3-minute drive to Central Plaza, which makes it a popular pick for people who don't want to pay a lot but also don't want to stay far from the centre. The best fit is budget travellers, people here for short work stays, families who want a big room at a light price, and drivers passing through who want free parking and easy check-in. Among the 10 hotels we reviewed, this one has the lightest starting price at about ฿650/night. It has several room tiers, and the thing guests mention repeatedly is that the rooms are bigger than expected at this price, especially the Triple and Suite rooms that fit several people for a small price difference. The rooms are plain and functional, with cold AC, a fridge, a flat-screen TV, free drinking water, and a fairly soft bed. There's on-site free parking, free Wi-Fi, a 24-hour reception, and front-desk staff reviews call friendly and helpful. The most repeated honest caveat is noise, since it's near bars and eateries — on some nights you hear the music in your room; the walls are fairly thin, so you may hear the next room and motorbikes from the street, some rooms look dated, and cleanliness is inconsistent. There's no pool, no fitness centre, and no big restaurant in the building, so if your trip involves a swim, look elsewhere. But if you're using the hotel just as a place to sleep while out exploring or working all day, B2 is a good-value pick that fits the budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you sleep lightly, ask for an upper-floor or interior room away from the street and not facing the bars, since that's the number-one complaint. If you're a group, go straight for a Triple or Suite — much bigger for a small price difference — and inspect the room at check-in; if it's not to your liking, you can ask to switch.

entries.addr: 43/2 Phimphasut Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen
entries.storyHtml: If you're after a downtown Khon Kaen stay on a budget, with an easy walk to the walking street and Ratchadanusorn Park, the name Khon Kaen Hotel often appears near the top of the list. Let's be straight up front: this isn't a new, stylishly designed hotel — it's a long-established downtown hotel that has stood with Khon Kaen for decades, open since 1980 with its last major renovation around 2010. Its charm lies in its downtown location and very accessible price, with entry-level rooms sometimes dropping below a thousand baht; the overall score of 8.7 from 167 Trip.com reviews is very respectable for a hotel at this price. The people it suits best are budget travellers who prioritise location over luxury, people here for short work or conference trips, and tourists who'd rather spend on food and sightseeing than the room. Location is the heart of it — the hotel is on Phimphasut Road in Nai Mueang, about a 5-minute walk from Ratchadanusorn Park and the Field Marshal Sarit Thanarat monument, and walkable to the Khon Kaen walking street about 500 metres away, ideal if you're here on a Saturday when the walking-street market is on. It has 125 rooms; the main room type is Superior, with both big beds and twin beds, and every room has AC, a TV, a minibar, a fridge, a work desk, and free Wi-Fi. There's the Pong Lang restaurant serving Thai and Isan food, a bar, a convenience store, a 24-hour front desk, and free parking that's rare for a downtown location like this. Service draws fairly steady praise, with friendly, helpful staff. Honest caveats: the building and some rooms are starting to age, the furniture is worn and due for an update, some rooms and bathrooms smell musty, the bathrooms are fairly small, the Wi-Fi signal isn't very stable, and breakfast has few options and is sometimes not hot. There's no pool, and there's an in-house bar, karaoke, and nightclub that can be noisy on some nights. If the brief is a downtown location within walking distance of everything at the most economical price, with warm local-hotel service, Khon Kaen Hotel is still a fitting choice.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a recently renovated or high-floor room right at booking, since condition varies. If you sleep lightly, request a room far from the bar, karaoke, and nightclub zone; bring a backup mobile data SIM in case the Wi-Fi isn't stable; and plan to visit on a Saturday when the walking street is on, since it's an easy walk.

entries.addr: 250-252 Si Chan Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen
entries.storyHtml: Ask people in Khon Kaen which hotel has stood with the city longest, and the name Kosa Hotel always floats up. It's a 4-star city hotel on Si Chan Road that has been open for decades, now rebranded as Kosa Hotel & Wellness Center with a newly refreshed wellness and fitness zone, scoring 8.2 from 584 reviews. The number-one strength almost no one disputes is location — the hotel connects directly to the in-house Kosa shopping mall, so you can step down from the lobby straight to the shops without going out in the sun; it's about a 5-minute walk to Central Plaza, and close to Khao Niao Road, with a location score on Booking as high as 9.2. The best fit is business travellers, people here on city business, those who want to enjoy the Khao Niao Road nightlife and walk back to their room, and families who want a hotel with a pool for the kids and plenty of parking. It has 197 rooms across several tiers, and reviews agree the rooms are bigger than expected, the beds are comfortable, and the linens and towels are nicely clean. The second strength praised in almost every review is the service — staff score 9-plus for being friendly, polite, and quick to help, with many saying they got a warm welcome from check-in and a fast check-in without a long wait. There's a large outdoor pool deep enough for real swimming with a separate kids' pool, a fitness centre, a sauna, a Thai-massage spa, a large snooker room, several restaurants including Kosa Coffee Shop, the Chinese restaurant Pai Liw, and a Beer Garden, plus free parking. Honest caveats from the reviews: the building and rooms are starting to age, the decor looks dated and some rooms could use an update, some bathrooms have weak water flow or seepage, window glass in some rooms isn't cleaned thoroughly, breakfast on some days has few options or the coffee and tea aren't hot, poolside umbrellas and chairs are limited when it's busy, and street-facing rooms may hear noise on Friday and Saturday nights. Bottom line — Kosa sells location and service, not a fresh building; if you want to be at the centre of everything in town on a low-thousands budget, it still fits.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a Deluxe room or higher and request a high-floor interior room for a clearly better and quieter room. Make the most of the mall-attached location by going down to eat, catch a movie, and shop in the mall and at Central without calling a ride, and if you sleep lightly, specify a room not facing the street.

entries.storyHtml: In a Khon Kaen where new hotels keep going up into tall towers and nudging prices higher every year, Green Hotel & Resort Khon Kaen still sits among the city stays that give you a big room at a light price, the kind that's getting hard to find. It's a 3-star city hotel on Prachasamoson Road, open since 2012 and with a major renovation in 2023, scoring an excellent 9.1 from 149 Trip.com reviews. To sum it up as briefly as possible, this is one of Khon Kaen's best at the room-space-per-baht game — it isn't a stylish design boutique and it isn't a luxury hotel with a rooftop pool, but it's all substance: big rooms, comfy beds, and a price that's easy on the wallet. The best fit is budget travellers who want lots of room space, families travelling in numbers, drivers who prioritise free parking, and groups attending a wedding or seminar in the hotel's own banquet halls. It has 78 rooms; standard rooms start at around 28 square metres, bigger than the same-class rooms at many city hotels that often give just over 20 sqm. Many rooms have a private balcony with laminate wood flooring, walls decorated with natural stone, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, free drinking water, and AC that reviews say cools quickly and strongly. Something guests especially like is the generous number of power outlets, letting you charge several devices at once — a detail many hotels overlook. There's free parking, a fresh-made breakfast buffet with Thai-Isan flavours many reviews praise, and 7 meeting and banquet halls for 30–700 people that locals in Khon Kaen favour for weddings and seminars. Honest caveats: there's no pool and no fitness centre, despite the word 'resort' in the name; water pressure in some bathrooms is weak; the room lighting is fairly dim, making it hard to read at night; some spots are starting to age despite the renovation; and the Prachasamoson location is about a 15-minute drive from Central, so you'll need a vehicle almost every time you go out. For drivers who measure value by room space against money in the pocket, every baht spent here comes back in full.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: This place suits drivers, with free parking and a location that needs a vehicle; use the hotel as a base to go eat Isan food around the city. If you're a group or staying long, choose the Deluxe or Suite with an extra sitting area, and if you're sensitive to light, ask for a brighter room or bring your own reading lamp.

entries.storyHtml: If you arrive in Khon Kaen by train and want a stay you can wheel your luggage to straight off the platform at a wallet-friendly price, SF Biz Hotel is a name budget travellers bring up often. It's a budget city hotel of around 3 stars on Drun Samran Road, with an unusual standout feature: it's decorated with a chicken-and-egg theme throughout the building — from the facade, lobby, and rooms to the restaurant, karaoke rooms, and meeting rooms. The owner touts it as the only chicken-and-egg hotel concept in Thailand, giving the place a clear, memorable character; it averages 7.0 from 856 Agoda reviews. The number-one selling point is location — the hotel sits in the city centre within walking distance of several key spots. It's about a 400-metre walk to Khon Kaen train station, so rail arrivals can wheel their luggage straight to the hotel without paying for onward transport — which is why some platforms list it as Khon Kaen Railway Favourite — and Central Plaza is about 900 metres, roughly a 10–12 minute walk, while Khon Kaen Airport is about a 10-minute drive. The best fit is rail travellers, budget-minded guests, business travellers here on short city trips, and anyone stopping a single night before moving on. There are about 150 rooms across several tiers, with AC, a fridge, a minibar, a TV, a water heater, and free Wi-Fi; there's fairly large free parking that reviews praise often, small and large meeting rooms, and karaoke rooms — the source of the 'Biz' in the name. The honest caveat that pulls the score down most is night-time noise from nearby late-night shops and cafes that runs late on some nights, and inconsistent room quality and cleanliness — entry-level rooms are fairly small and dated, water pressure is weak in some, and some guests found insects in the room; on the other hand, some reviews who stayed in a renovated room said it was cleaner and more charmingly decorated than expected for the price. There's no pool and no proper fitness centre. If you see a hotel as a place to crash near the station and the mall for a few hundred baht, this fits that brief well.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a renovated room or a Queen Suite right at booking, since room quality varies. If you sleep lightly, request an interior or high-floor room not facing the street, since this area has late-night spots that get loud on some nights; check the cleanliness of the room and bed right when you walk in; and confirm clearly whether the package includes breakfast.

entries.storyHtml: If you want to get away from downtown Khon Kaen to sleep to the sound of the river, look out at the mountains, and wake to coffee by the water, Varee Valley Resort and Restaurant is a name people exploring the Ubolratana Dam area bring up often. It's a small resort in Ubolratana District, Ban Dong, set on the Nam Phong river, open since 2014 with a major renovation in 2020, scoring 7.6 and 4.1 on TripAdvisor, ranked around #28 of 76 hotels in Khon Kaen. To sum it up as briefly as possible, this is a riverside resort for people who want to leave the city to recharge, more than a hotel in town. It isn't a tower you can walk to a mall from and it isn't a luxury 5-star resort, but it sells the atmosphere of the Nam Phong amid gardens and a mountain backdrop, with a white English-style cafe as a magnet drawing people to stop for photos. You need to understand the location before booking, because the resort is in Ubolratana District, not downtown Khon Kaen — you have to drive about 50 kilometres north, taking roughly 50 minutes to 1 hour. The upside is that once you arrive, you're on the Nam Phong, only about a 5-minute drive from Ubolratana Dam and the Ubolratana golf course, and near Wat Phra Bat Phu Phan Kham, a viewpoint over the dam. It suits people with their own car best, since there's no convenient public transport around the resort. The right fit is road-tripping families, couples who want a quiet sleep by the water, golfers playing the Ubolratana course, and people following the trail of photogenic cafes. It has 36 rooms in several styles; the most recommended group is the River View rooms that open straight onto the Nam Phong, with many reviews saying the extra cost is worth it for the full atmosphere. The decor leans warm vintage mixed with woodwork. The star that has made the name known beyond the resort itself is the white English-style cafe with a spiral staircase up to a rooftop, a popular check-in photo spot, and the riverside restaurant that many TripAdvisor reviews praise as tasty, fairly priced, with big plates; breakfast is included in the room rate. There's a riverside garden, a playground, a seminar room, free parking, and staff reviews call friendly and kind in the style of an up-country family resort. Honest caveats: there's no pool; some rooms are starting to age, the beds are fairly firm for some people, being a nature-side riverside resort there are some ants and insects, bathroom cleanliness is inconsistent in spots, and some complain the outdoor path lights shine into the room at night. For a slow riverside getaway near the dam, Varee Valley has a charm of its own in the Ubolratana zone.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you value the view and atmosphere, go straight for a River View room — that's the best value of the resort. This place suits people with a car; save the map pin and the resort's phone number before you set off, since the final stretch of road runs through a village, and if you're sensitive to light, ask about the outdoor path lights or bring an eye mask.

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates from the standard-room range and may change by date and season; we recommend checking the real price and comparing 3 sites before every booking. The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms, not from staying ourselves. The Heritage Grand Khon Kaen is the former Pullman Raja Orchid building, rebranded — old and new reviews are mixed, so focus on the latest reviews. Avani Khon Kaen was formerly a Pullman before joining the Avani group. During the city's major events (the Khon Kaen Silk Fair and Phuk Siao tradition in Nov–Dec, and the Khon Kaen University graduation period), rooms fill fast and prices rise, so book ahead. Khon Kaen has no metro; Grab or songthaew is convenient, and it's about a 10–15 min drive from the airport into the city. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common questions travellers ask about hotels in Khon Kaen

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best popular hotel in Khon Kaen?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. Measured by score and luxury, Avani Khon Kaen has the highest score in this article at 9.5, a 5-star hotel with a large convention centre. Measured by value for a big room, Green Hotel & Resort scores 9.1 with rooms from ~28 sqm at ฿850. For downtown location and service, Kosa Hotel is attached to a mall with a service score of 9.1. If you arrive by train, Glacier or SF Biz are within walking distance of the station. And if you want to escape the city to the water, Varee Valley Resort is near Ubolratana Dam.

faq.q: ❓ How much do hotels in Khon Kaen cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at about ฿650–2,000 per night. On the budget side: B2 Khon Kaen from ฿650, SF Biz from ฿700, Khon Kaen Hotel from ฿731, and Green Hotel & Resort from ฿850. Mid-range: Glacier ฿1,000, Charoen Thani and Kosa ฿1,100. And at the top end of this article: Avani ฿1,600, Varee Valley ฿1,400, and The Heritage Grand ฿2,000. All prices are approximate starting rates from standard rooms; during city events prices may be higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Khon Kaen?
faq.a: Si Chan Road / Khao Niao Road in the city centre, good for nightlife and shopping, walk to Central and the nightlife zone (Charoen Thani, Kosa) · Prachasamoson Road / Prachasamran Road, near the centre but away from the bustle, with plenty of parking (Avani, The Heritage Grand, Glacier, Green Hotel) · near the train station, good if you arrive by rail (Glacier, SF Biz, Khon Kaen Hotel) · and Ubolratana District, out of town to the north, for a resort by the dam (Varee Valley), which needs a vehicle.

faq.q: ❓ Are The Heritage Grand and Pullman Raja Orchid the same place?
faq.a: Yes, it's the same building on Prachasamran Road, which originally opened as the Pullman Khon Kaen Raja Orchid and, after changing ownership and rebranding, reopened as The Heritage Grand Khon Kaen Hotel and Convention. The structure and room sizes are unchanged, but the management and service changed hands. When reading reviews, focus on the latest ones after the name change for an accurate current picture. As for Avani Khon Kaen, it too was formerly a Pullman before joining the Avani group — a different building.

faq.q: ❓ Which Khon Kaen hotel is good for families and has a pool?
faq.a: The most family-friendly with a pool are Avani Khon Kaen, with a kids' pool with a slide, and Kosa Hotel, with a big pool plus a separate kids' pool and attached to a mall. Next are Charoen Thani, with an outdoor pool and big rooms that sleep several, and Glacier, with an indoor pool. B2, SF Biz, Khon Kaen Hotel, Green Hotel, and Varee Valley have no pool.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Khon Kaen hotel?
faq.a: In normal periods, booking 1–3 weeks ahead is enough. But during the city's major events, such as the Khon Kaen Silk Fair and Phuk Siao tradition (November–December) and the Khon Kaen University graduation period, downtown rooms fill very fast and prices rise quickly, so book a month or more ahead, especially downtown hotels like Kosa, Charoen Thani, and Avani. Every platform has Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in a rate that way if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
